title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
requirement: Landlords are prohibited from terminating tenancies without just cause and must provide relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
coverage_conditions: residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
exemptions: transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner’s roommate, cooperatives, some non-profit facilities for the homeless, short-term treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government
quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower.
exemptions: units constructed within the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, certain dormitories, owner-occupied two-unit properties, and certain single-family homes/condos
interaction: The JCO does not regulate rent increases, however, state law AB 1482, the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019, may regulate the rent amount in buildings that are older than 15 years old.
quoted_span: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).

title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent
requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant for non-payment of rent unless the amount owed is higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit size.
citation: Section: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent
quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
